body:
Adding The Klingon Journal of Battle as an official academic publication track under Stichting Attogram gives the foundation a distinct open-access research outlet.
In Klingon lore, Battle (May') extends beyond hand-to-hand combat; it encompasses intellectual struggle, scientific discovery, and overcoming complex engineering or philosophical challenges. Publishing serious multidisciplinary research alongside parallel tlhIngan Hol (Klingon) translations mirrors the protocol's commitment to continuous, unmoderated public scholarship.
attogram.019: The Klingon Journal of Battle (may' 'laH qeS)
 * The Concept: An open-access, peer-kibitzed academic journal published under Stichting Attogram. It accepts research papers across all disciplines—from AI curriculum design to urban ecology—and pairs every accepted submission with an open-source, community-driven translation into Klingon (tlhIngan Hol), while maintaining its original multilingual text.
 * Core Mechanics:
   * No Static Volumes or Expiration: True to the Perpetual Petition Protocol, papers are not grouped into static "issues." Every accepted paper is assigned a permanent, immutable DOI (e.g., attogram.019.001, attogram.019.002).
   * Continuous Open Peer Review ("Kibitzing"): Formal peer review takes place asynchronously on the paper's permanent public thread. Revisions, mathematical proofs, and translation improvements are logged as continuous updates without closing the paper.
   * Multilingual & tlhIngan Hol Corpus: Authors submit papers in English, Dutch, or their native language. The community and automated SLMs work on the parallel Klingon translation, creating a specialized parallel corpus for linguistic AI research.
